h1: Carpet Cleaning Marketing for Multi-Crew Companies
intro: Carpet cleaning marketing for a multi-crew company has two jobs: win new residential and commercial customers, and bring them back on schedule. ASP runs SEO, Local Services Ads, Google and Facebook ads, and repeat-customer follow-up for larger carpet cleaning companies, measured against booked jobs.

sections.heading: How carpet cleaning demand works
paragraphs: Carpet cleaning is recurring work. The Carpet and Rug Institute (CRI) recommends professional cleaning every 12 to 18 months for both homes and businesses, or more often if needed. That interval sets your marketing calendar, because every finished job starts the clock on the next one.

Commercial accounts come with their own standards. CRI publishes CRI 204, a commercial carpet maintenance and cleaning standard for business facilities, and the ANSI/IICRC S100 standard sets procedures for professional cleaning of commercial and residential carpet and rugs. The 2021 seventh edition of S100 is current, and a revision is under way.

Most carpet cleaning businesses are small. In 2023, Census counted 6,673 carpet and upholstery cleaning establishments with paid employees, and 4,829 had fewer than five employees, while 256 had 20 to 49 and 47 had 50 to 99. A company running several crews has more to show a buyer: a wider service area, commercial capacity and certified technicians if your team holds the credential.

sections.heading: Channels ASP runs for carpet cleaning companies
paragraphs: Carpet cleaning services is one of Google's Local Services Ads categories in the US, in areas where Google runs it. Placement comes from an auction that looks at your bid and your profile quality, which covers your rating, number of reviews, average response time, high-quality photos and completed verification checks. With several crews finishing jobs, a review request after every job keeps that profile growing.

On the organic side, we build separate pages for each service you sell, such as carpet, upholstery, rugs and commercial maintenance, and keep your Google Business Profile current in every area your crews cover.

Google Search Ads catch the homeowner dealing with a stain or a move-out today. Facebook and Instagram fit a low-ticket recurring service well, because a seasonal offer can sell directly to past customers and to the neighborhoods you already serve.

sections.heading: Trust signals carpet cleaning buyers check
paragraphs: CRI's consumer hiring guidance suggests asking whether a cleaner's technicians are IICRC certified and how long the company has been in business. Those answers belong on your website, your Business Profile and your ads.

Manufacturer warranties are another reason to show credentials. CRI says carpet manufacturers recommend, and sometimes require, Seal of Approval certified cleaners for warranty protection. Cleaners who use Seal of Approval solutions with Seal of Approval equipment can be recognized as Seal of Approval service providers, and a company can apply to become an IICRC Certified Firm with at least one IICRC Certified Technician, proof of general liability insurance and a $25 application fee.

sections.heading: Repeat customers and how we measure them
paragraphs: The first job gets credited to the channel that brought the customer in. Every repeat cleaning after that counts as retention and gets credited to your follow-up, not to the original ad. Mixing the two makes acquisition look better than it is and hides customers who stopped coming back.

If you run Housecall Pro, which lists carpet cleaning among its industries, we build reminders, win-back messages and review requests on HCP's job events so each one fires from real activity. HCP attribution setup is part of the Foundation tier, and the monthly report shows new-customer jobs and revenue by channel.

sections.heading: What you own
paragraphs: In a recurring business, the customer list is the asset that pays you again and again, and it stays yours. So do the website and domain, your Google Business Profile and reviews, your ad accounts and the reminder and follow-up automations we build. If you leave, ASP charges no handover or exit fee to move any of it.

faqs.question: Can a carpet cleaning company with several locations run Local Services Ads?
faqs.answer: Yes, where Google offers the category. Google asks businesses serving multiple locations for business- and employee-level licenses for each location where licenses apply. When one business has several locations serving the same area, Local Services shows only the highest-ranking ad, so coverage areas need planning before the profiles go live.

faqs.question: How often should we remind customers to book again?
faqs.answer: CRI recommends professional cleaning every 12 to 18 months for homes and businesses, more often if needed. That interval is a sensible starting point for reminder timing, and your own repeat-booking data should set the final schedule.

faqs.question: Do you market commercial carpet cleaning?
faqs.answer: Yes. Commercial pages and ads are written for facility buyers and name the standards your crews follow, such as CRI 204 for commercial carpet maintenance and ANSI/IICRC S100 for cleaning procedures.
